market_summary: W35 reversed. Price reached 4,697.07 on Tuesday - a new high for the rebound and effectively the target band both producers' prior-week reports had named - then fell away, and Friday alone dropped 148.42 points (-3.20%), the largest single-day fall in four weeks. The week closed at 4,453.67, only 3.2% up from the weekly low of 4,445.546, the weakest weekly close in a month. The dollar index rose over the same three days from 99.129 to a weekly high of 99.726, closing 99.677, so the fall lines up in time with dollar strength rather than with a purely technical unwind. Short-term momentum is now deeply oversold - 30m RSI 21.62, 1h RSI 22.37 - while the daily and weekly RSI are still neutral at 54.55 and 52.89. Price has lost the 4h 50 EMA at 4,547.46, but the daily 50 and 200 EMAs at 4,334.78 and 4,307.59 remain far below, so the daily-scale uptrend is not yet threatened. Positioning as of the 08-25 report date still shows managed money net long 144,747 contracts, up 3,099 on the week - but that cutoff falls before the sell-off, so it cannot show whether crowded longs have begun to unwind.

agreements: Both independent reports were built from the same frozen automated run and the same finalized primary chart snapshot, so their evidence identity is shared and a claim-by-claim comparison is eligible for multi-source publication.

Both report identical market facts: W35 close 4,453.67, weekly high 4,697.07, weekly low 4,445.546; dollar index close 99.677; gold RSI 21.62 (30m), 22.37 (1h), 31.72 (4h); dollar index RSI 76.56 (1h) and 75.03 (4h).

Both transcribed the 2026-08-25 positioning report directly from the same official image and matched the official CSV on all seven fields: open interest 427,957 (+21,697), managed money long 159,819 (+5,224), short 15,072 (+2,125), spread 16,251 (+660), net long 144,747 (+3,099).

Both record the same macro gap honestly: the real-rate, 10-year yield, volatility and gold-volatility inputs have no source newer than 2026-06-18, so a complete macro verdict is unavailable and neither report carried stale values forward as if fresh.
Both identify 4,471.67 - the lower edge of the unfilled 4h bearish imbalance left by the fall - as the first resistance a bounce has to clear.
Both place the week's decision zone at roughly 4,442-4,454, and both note price has lost the 4h 50 EMA while the daily moving-average structure is still intact well below.
Both independently determined the same employment-release date and the same hard pre-release close time, reached by separate calendar checks rather than by copying each other.
Both end on the same stance: no new position early in the week, and every entry, stop and target reconfirmed on a live chart after the open.
disagreements: Directional weighting, and the largest split in this edition: one report reads bullish 35 / range 35 / bearish 30, the other bearish 45 / range 35 / bullish 20. Both assign range the same 35, so only the directional half is contested. Neither figure is a measured frequency - both are judgements formed from the same readings - so they were not averaged. The published ordering follows the more conservative reading, supported by two directly verifiable facts: the week closed 3.2% off its low in the bottom of its own range, and price has lost the 4h 50 EMA. The opposing bullish-leaning reading is not refuted and is recorded as unresolved.

The lower edge of the decision zone was derived differently: one report used 4,445.546, the price that actually traded as the weekly low, the other 4,442.30, a computed 1h lower Bollinger band. They sit 3.25 points apart - well inside the 30m ATR of 29.18 - so price cannot separate them and they were merged into one zone. The traded low is still published separately inside that zone, because a price where trading actually occurred accumulates resting orders in a way a computed band does not.

Breakout strategy grading: one report declined to publish entry and stop numbers at all, judging the setup too far away to price; the other graded it a distant conditional and published entry 4,605.00 with stop 4,583.90. Both agree exactly on the trigger condition - a 4h close reclaiming the 4,584.16-4,602.66 pivot plus a fresh formal signal - so the condition was adopted and neither grade letter was. The published stop carries an explicit warning: 21.10 points is 0.45x the 4h ATR of 46.48, narrower than ordinary noise.

Event coverage differed materially: one report listed only the Friday employment release, the other listed five events with official schedule citations. The fuller list was adopted on source directness, not on producer preference - it cites the statistical agency's own September schedule page and the survey publisher's stated release rule. Two of those five, the Tuesday job-openings release and the Friday employment release, were independently re-verified while preparing this publication; the remaining three are carried on the cited official sources, which could not be re-read directly from this environment.

recommendation.summary: Wait. The week ended with a sharp reversal that closed near its own low and below the 4h 50 EMA, while short-term momentum is deeply oversold and the daily-scale trend is still intact - a combination that argues for letting the first move after the open resolve rather than anticipating it. The 4,442.30-4,453.67 zone is the decision point: holding it opens the recovery case, losing it opens continuation. The breakout strategy is roughly 151 points away and is not a live setup; the reversal strategy is observation-only until a fresh live signal appears in that zone. The week is also front-loaded with releases and ends in a Friday employment report, which forces a full close by Thursday 22:00 Taipei.
recommendation.invalidation: An hourly close below 4,442.30 that the bounce cannot reclaim shifts the week to continuation; a 4h close back above 4,495.02, and then 4,523.77-4,557.51, shifts it to recovery.

evidence_limits: The two independent reports share one frozen evidence identity and are compared claim by claim. Agreement is stated only where both reports actually support the claim; where they differ on judgement, the difference is published rather than smoothed.

The directional probability split was left unresolved rather than averaged. The published ordering follows the more conservative of two defensible readings and is a judgement, not an agreed figure - the opposing reading is recorded and is not refuted.

Positioning data carries a 2026-08-25 report date, before the 08-26 to 08-28 sell-off. It therefore cannot show whether crowded long positions have started to unwind, and the net long figure of 144,747 must not be read as current crowding.

Real rate, 10-year yield, equity volatility and gold volatility inputs have no source newer than 2026-06-18 and are recorded as unknown rather than carried forward from stale values. This gap has now persisted across several editions.

Three of the four listed events are carried on the official sources cited by one producer and could not be re-read directly from the publishing environment; the job-openings and employment releases were independently re-verified.

The source-comparison history has reached 6 of the 8 valid weekly observations required, so automated source confidence remains insufficient_history and the alternate feed cannot be promoted to a formal source.
All levels are weekend reference values computed from the last close. They are not live quotes, and a gap at the open can invalidate the assumed ranges and reward-to-risk.
disclaimer: Research evidence, not trading advice. Live chart confirmation is required before execution.
language_note: Both source reports for this edition were written in Traditional Chinese; this public summary is an English rendering of their reviewed aggregate content, not a verbatim translation of either report.
